hooks.text: Astronomers first saw a faint violet speck, calling it an ordinary star.
This faint blue dot is actually heavier than forty billion Suns.
A tiny photographic speck hid a shadow forty times wider than Pluto's orbit.

title: The Faint Blue Star That Held 40 Billion Suns
description: Mistaken for an ordinary faint star in 1957, TON 618 turned out to be an ultramassive black hole outshining 140 trillion Suns.

beats.text: Astronomers first saw a faint violet speck, calling it an ordinary star.
beats.visual: Historical photographic survey plate showing faint stars from Tonantzintla Observatory, 1957

beats.text: In 1957, astronomers catalogued it as entry 618, unaware of what lurked 10.8 billion light-years away.
beats.visual: Portrait of astronomers Braulio Iriarte and Enrique Chavira, 1950s

beats.text: That point of light is an ultramassive black hole spanning 1,300 astronomical units across.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a supermassive black hole with an accretion disk, NASA, 2019

beats.text: That is 40 times Pluto’s distance from the Sun, all swallowed into one dark sphere.
beats.visual: Diagram comparing the event horizon of TON 618 to the orbit of Pluto, 2020
queries: Black hole size comparison solar system

beats.text: Gas whipping around at 10,000 kilometers per second fuels the brilliance of 140 trillion Suns.
beats.visual: Animation of gas spinning at relativistic speeds around a black hole, NASA, 2014

beats.text: Early estimates suggested 66 billion solar masses, later revised down to 40.7 billion.
beats.visual: Astronomical chart showing broad emission lines used to calculate quasar mass, 2018

beats.text: Encircled by a glowing nebula 300,000 light-years wide, it remains one of the heaviest singular objects known.
beats.visual: Artist impression of an enormous Lyman-alpha nebula surrounding a quasar, ESO, 2016

beats.text: Yet from billions of light-years away, this universe-swallowing giant still hides in plain sight.
beats.visual: Deep wide-field photograph of the night sky showing distant background stars, 2021

better_than_last: Trimmed beat 2 and removed repetitive mass terminology in beat 6 to bring runtime safely under the 58-second upper bound.
